content.body:
The Bell Model 14A was the first export version of the P-39 Airacobra. A mid-engine design and quick controls gave the P-39 a fairly unstable flight profile and earned it a reputation as a hot ship with a quick temper. While anemic at higher altitudes, it was very fast in low level flight and practically unmatchable in a dive. France ordered hundreds of these at the same time they ordered the P-38 and P-40 designs under various export sales programs prior to their eventual real life surrender late in 1940.
A single centerline mounted 20mm cannon along with two .50 cal guns mounted in the cowling and an additional four .30 cal guns in the wings, the Iron Dog carried more than enough firepower to handle a dogfight, but its delicate performance regime proved difficult to handle for most USAAF combat pilots. This limerick was penned by USAAF fighter pilots early in the Airacobras deployment:
..."don't give me a P-39 the engine is mounted behind she'll tumble spin she'll auger you in don't give me a P-39"bell14a handlers/unit
